title: Operational Innovation Lab and Postmortem Prioritization Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook describes the Operational Innovation Lab (OIL) process and the postmortem prioritization framework used by Platform Engineering to convert high-severity incidents, recurring reliability issues, and cost-inefficient patterns into measurable engineering work that improves SLOs and platform economics. It defines roles, scoring criteria, minimally viable experiment (MVE) patterns, and the handoff into roadmap/OKR planning.

Why this doc exists
- Reduce time-to-impact for fixes discovered via incidents and retrospectives.
- Ensure consistent prioritization between reliability, cost, and product impact.
- Create a repeatable experimentation path from detection -> hypothesis -> MVE -> measurement -> rollout.

Scope
This playbook applies to platform services owned by eng-platform including but not limited to: routing & orchestrator, prefix/KV cache, batching service, GPU pool manager, tenant slicing, telemetry plumbing, and cost attribution. It does not replace normal feature planning for product-facing work; it supplements incident-derived work and targeted innovation experiments.

Goals & Success Criteria
- 80% of postmortem action items are either closed or have an active MVE in progress within 30 days.
- Median time from incident to MVE deployment <= 14 days for P0/P1 incidents.
- Demonstrable improvements instrumented in dashboards (SLO delta, token cost savings, or reduced tail-latency) after rollout.

Roles & Responsibilities
- Incident Lead: owns the postmortem and the "Problem Statement" artifact; triggers OIL intake.
- Platform Innovation Owner (PIO): engineering lead who shepherds the action item into OIL, authors prioritization inputs.
- Experiment Sponsor: product or reliability PM who accepts metrics and success criteria.
- Operator Owner: SRE/Platform engineer responsible for runbook and operationalization.
- Release/QA Owner: ensures canary/testing gates are defined and executed.
- OIL Committee: cross-functional reviewers (Platform, Runtime, SRE, Observability, Cost) who meet weekly to score and accept experiments into the 2-week sprint of OIL work.

Operational flow (high-level)
1) Incident -> Postmortem creation (standard template).
2) PIO converts action item into an OIL intake card with hypothesis and proposed MVE.
3) OIL Committee scores intake using the prioritization rubric below.
4) If accepted, experiment goes into OIL sprint cadence with explicit measurement plan and owner.
5) MVE -> Canary -> Measure -> Decide: rollback, iterate, or promote to roadmap.

Intake checklist (required fields for an OIL card)
- Title (concise)
- Problem statement (1-2 sentences)
- Observed impact: SLO breaches, customer incidents, cost delta, or security exposure
- Repro steps or telemetry pointers (links to traces/dashboards)
- Proposed MVE (scope, systems touched, estimated owner and effort)
- Success criteria (metric and a target)
- Rollback plan and safety gates
- Estimated engineering effort (T-shirt: S, M, L)

Prioritization rubric (scoring)
Each intake is scored 0-5 on the following axes. The total is a sum; OIL Committee uses thresholds to accept or decline. Use integer values.
- Customer Impact (0-5): number of impacted customers and business criticality.
- Recurrence Risk (0-5): probability the issue recurs without intervention.
- SLO Delta (0-5): expected improvement to SLI/SLO (latency, error rate, availability).
- Cost Savings (0-5): expected token/GPU/capacity cost reduction in 90 days.
- Regulatory/Compliance Risk (0-5): severity if applicable.
- Engineering Effort Inverse (0-5): 5 = trivial (<1d), 0 = multi-sprint.
- Observability Gap Reduction (0-5): how much better we can detect or prevent similar incidents.

Scoring example (ASCII table)
+-------------------------------+-----+
| Axis                          | Score|
+-------------------------------+-----+
| Customer Impact               | 4   |
| Recurrence Risk               | 5   |
| SLO Delta                     | 3   |
| Cost Savings                  | 2   |
| Regulatory Risk               | 0   |
| Effort Inverse                | 3   |
| Observability Gap Reduction   | 4   |
+-------------------------------+-----+
| TOTAL                         | 21  |
+-------------------------------+-----+
Threshold guidance: totals >= 20 -> accept; 12-19 -> conditional/fast-track with mitigations; <12 -> deprioritize or require stronger business case. Adjust thresholds quarterly.

MVE templates (pick one)
- Configuration Fix MVE (1-3 days): apply a constrained config change behind a feature flag + 24h canary + automated rollback.
- Routing Policy Patch (3-7 days): small refactor to routing heuristics with unit tests, canary traffic slice, and SLI instrumentation.
- Cache Prefetch/TTL Adjustment (3 days): implement TTL tuning and measure hit rate improvement and downstream token cost reduction.
- Query-level Batching Tweak (5-10 days): batching window/heuristic change instrumented with per-tenant metrics.

Canary and Safety Gates
- Every OIL experiment must define a canary slice (tenant or region) and an automated abort if any of the following occur:
  - Error rate spike > 2x baseline for 5m
  - Tail latency P99 exceeds target by > 30% for 10m
  - Token cost per request increases by > 10% compared to baseline for 1h
- Canary duration defaults: 24h for config-only changes, 72h for routing/serving changes. Longer for multi-region.

Measurement plan (examples)
- Baseline capture: snapshot the primary SLI (e.g., inference P95 latency, error rate, tokens per request, GPU utilization) for 7 days prior.
- Experiment measurement: compare rolling 24h windows during canary vs baseline; use bootstrap CI for small-sample tenants.
- Acceptance criteria: must meet both SLO delta and not regress any critical metric for the canary slice for the defined duration.

Instrumentation & Dashboarding guidance
When an OIL experiment is accepted, the owner must create/update the following dashboards before canary:
- Experiment Overview: primary metric, comparison to baseline, and canary slice breakdown.
- Cost Impact Dashboard: per-tenant token consumption, estimated token spend delta, GPU-hours.
- Rollback Triggers: single-pane view of the automated abort conditions.
- Observability Gap Map: list of telemetry missing or added by the experiment.
Include links to the dashboards in the OIL card. Suggested metrics/alerts:
- SLI: inference P95, P99, error-rate, prefix cache hit-rate, model-serving queue length.
- Cost: tokens per request, GPU utilization by model-version, tenant-level spend rate.
- Operator health: restarts, eviction rates, container OOMs.

Runbook handoffs (operationalization)
If an experiment is promoted to roadmap, the PIO must deliver:
1) A canonical runbook for the change describing symptoms, mitigation steps, rollback, and telemetry anchors.
2) A scheduled 2-week monitoring window after full rollout with daily check-ins documented in the runbook.
3) A deprecation/cleanup task list for temporary flags or metrics.

Roadmap & OKR integration
- Quarterly planning: OIL publishes the list of promoted experiments and their measured ROI. Engineering leadership reserves at least one sprint per quarter for high-impact OIL promotions (target: 10-20% of platform capacity).
- Metrics feeding roadmap: acceptance rate, median time to MVE, and realized SLO/cost delta. These should be presented in the platform roadmap update deck.

Ops bounty program (incentivization)
To increase cross-team participation, we run an ops bounty program:
- Bounty awards for closed OIL experiments that show measurable impact. Awards types: public recognition, small spot bonuses, or training credit.
- Nomination process: any engineer or oncall can nominate a contributor; OIL Committee validates impact before awarding.
- Tracking: maintain an Ops Bounty board (kanban) with all nominations and award status.

Example case study (unique)
Title: "Prefix cache evictions causing burst P99s for small tenants"
- Symptom: sudden P99 spikes during high-concurrency bursts affecting 12 paying tenants.
- Postmortem finding: aggressive shard eviction policy combined with a long-tail of short-lived requests.
- Proposed MVE: change eviction threshold for small-tenant bins + add LRU hysteresis + instrument per-tenant cache hit-rate metric.
- Scoring: Customer Impact=4, Recurrence=4, SLO Delta=4, Cost Savings=1, Effort Inv=3, Observability=5 -> TOTAL=21 (accepted).
- Execution: config feature-flagged change applied to 5 low-risk tenants for 72h canary; hit-rate improved 27%, P99 dropped 42% for canary tenants; promoted to gradual rollout over 2 weeks.
- Outcome: after promotion, median P99 across cluster reduced from 420ms -> 245ms; rollback never triggered.

Templates & CLI snippets
- OIL card creation (CLI example):
  redwood-oil create --title "reduce-prefix-eviction-hysteresis" --owner maya.chen --estimate S --hypothesis "increase small-tenant cache TTL will decrease P99 by >30%" --dashboards "/dashboards/prefix-cache-hit-rate"
- Quick query (observability) example (pseudo-QL):
  SELECT tenant_id, p99_latency, cache_hit_rate FROM inference_metrics WHERE timeframe = last_7_days ORDER BY p99_latency DESC LIMIT 20

Governance & cadence
- Weekly OIL Committee meetings: intake review, scoring, and acceptance decisions. Documented approvals required for acceptance.
- Monthly ops-bounty retrospective: review awarded experiments, celebrate wins, and surface systemic blockers.
- Quarterly threshold reassessment: adjust scoring weights and acceptance thresholds based on backlog and capacity.

Success measurement & reporting
- Dashboards to report: OIL acceptance rate, time-to-mve, % experiments promoted to roadmap, aggregate SLO improvement, and monthly platform cost delta attributable to promotions.
- Report cadence: weekly snapshot to eng-platform, monthly highlight to execs during roadmap review.

Appendix: scoring weight recommendation (reference)
We recommend the following weights when comparing different axes for manual tie-breaks:
- Customer Impact: 1.5x
- Recurrence Risk: 1.25x
- SLO Delta: 1.5x
- Cost Savings: 1.0x
- Regulatory Risk: 2.0x (if non-zero)
- Effort Inverse: 0.8x
- Observability: 1.2x

Related pages & references
